Burke Wealth Management, an investment management company, released its "Focused Growth Strategy" Q3 2026 investor letter. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here. The fund delivered strong results in the third quarter of 2026, benefiting from a sharp recovery in enterprise software and solid corporate earnings amid continued market volatility. The composite returned 10.8% net of fees, substantially outperforming the S&P 500 Total Return Index's 2.3% gain, while its year-to-date return reached 20.0%, compared with 12.7% for the benchmark. The firm attributed the quarter's strength partly to investors reassessing the long-term value of enterprise software platforms that can securely connect AI models with proprietary business data. Burke believes these platforms can serve as essential AI "harnesses," providing permissions, security, and context for enterprise applications, although it cautions that AI agents could challenge traditional software business models and seat-based pricing. Looking ahead, Burke remains optimistic about the remainder of 2026, citing strong corporate earnings growth and the transition from AI infrastructure investment toward practical applications that may improve productivity and consumer experiences. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

In its second-quarter 2026 investor letter, Burke Wealth Focused Growth Strategy highlighted stocks like Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT). Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) is a global retail company that operates discount stores, supermarkets, and e-commerce platforms while expanding its digital and advertising businesses. The one-month return of Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) was 10.74% while its shares traded between $98.88 and $135.16 over the last 52 weeks. On October 23, 2026, Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) stock closed at approximately $119.89 per share, with a market capitalization of about $954.07 billion.

WMT trades near $122 with a ~$967 billion market cap, just short of $1 trillion, fueled by investors paying ~40x forward earnings, a notable rise from the 35x multiple seen in late September.

Walmart is funding 11,000+ price rollbacks using $2.9 billion in tariff refunds, a bet CEO John Furner says "drives market share gains over time."

The Nov. 19 earnings report lands between Walmart's two Black Friday sales, giving investors their first read on holiday momentum before results arrive.

Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) announced three holiday shopping events on Oct. 26, with its stock close to a $1 trillion market value. As of 10:25 a.m. ET, shares traded at $121.59. That was up 1.42% on the day, 10.01% over the past month and 9.83% year to date, for a market value of about $966.67 billion.

2012 Getty Images / Getty Images News via Getty Images

Investors may be counting on a strong holiday season to carry Walmart past $1 trillion. Available sources link the rally to other factors. TIKR attributes the move to investors paying a higher valuation multiple, and TipRanks linked the Oct. 22 gain to comments from an Oppenheimer analyst. That puts a lot of weight on the holidays, because a richer valuation needs profit growth to back it up.
